rows.what: 100,000 rows, each with two numbers and three formulas (arithmetic, IF, ROUND), loaded and computed.
In that workbook, one number in row 50,001 changes, and the three formulas on its row recompute.

rows.workload: edit a cell read by 100,000 formulas
rows.what: Cell A1 is read by 100,000 formulas (=B1*$A$1+1 and so on); A1 changes and every formula recomputes. This is a full recalculation.
A1 is 1 and each cell below adds 1 to the cell above it (=A1+1, =A2+1, ...), 100,000 cells deep.

rows.workload: edit the start of a chain of 100,000
rows.what: In that chain, A1 changes, so all 100,000 cells below it recompute in order.
200 formulas =SUM(A1:A90000), =SUM(A2:A90001) and so on, over 100,000 numbers.
Each of 20,000 rows sums everything above it and itself: =SUM($A$1:A1), =SUM($A$1:A2) and so on.
2,000 formulas =VLOOKUP(E1,$A$1:$B$100000,2,FALSE) over 100,000 keys in no order.
2,000 formulas =VLOOKUP(E1,$A$1:$B$100000,2,TRUE) over 100,000 sorted keys; each key falls between two.
2,000 formulas =MATCH(E1,$A$1:$A$100000,0) over 100,000 keys in no order.
2,000 formulas =MATCH(E1,$A$1:$A$100000,1) over 100,000 sorted keys.
2,000 formulas =XLOOKUP(E1,$A$1:$A$100000,$B$1:$B$100000) over 100,000 keys in no order.
200 formulas =SUMIFS($A$1:$A$100000,$B$1:$B$100000,E1,$C$1:$C$100000,F1), each with its own pair of criteria such as "k3" and ">37".
200 formulas =COUNTIFS($B$1:$B$100000,E1,$C$1:$C$100000,F1) on the same data.
100,000 formulas =UPPER(LEFT(A1,6))&"-"&LEN(TRIM(A1))&"-"&SUBSTITUTE(A1,"a","o") over short texts.

rows.workload: insert a row near the top
rows.what: In the workbook of 300,000 formulas, one row is inserted above row 2, so every formula below it moves and its references change.
The memory the engine holds after the load and first compute of that workbook, in MB.
